reason: The text explicitly names two characters: Shiphrah (שִׁפְרָה) and Puah (פּוּעָה), described as Hebrew midwives (מְיַלְּדוֹת הָעִבְרִיּוֹת). These are ordinary women with a regular occupation, not royalty, prophets, or major biblical figures. While they show moral courage in fearing God and refusing Pharaoh's decree, their fundamental characterization is as regular people performing their daily work as midwives.
